name: @corvus-dsh/dsh-memory
description: Capability memory for DSH: mine finished sessions into four cognitive layers (facts with seq pointers, experiences, negative paths, structured SKILL.md skills), and filter lexical retrieval with a cheap LLM relevance pass. Reads the handoff ledger as a file contract; imports nothing from the slicing plugin.
notes: Decoupling contract: reads .retired.json / .transferred.json from the slicing plugin's dataDir. No code import in either direction.
v0.18.0: those ledgers are read as epoch envelopes. A newer writer's epoch, or an envelope with no payload, is REFUSED (reported as ledger.deferred) instead of being half-understood.
Skills are written as structured SKILL.md (frontmatter with when_to_use + 执行步骤 + 验证标准) into the DSH skill directory, so the next generation picks them up with no plugin installed.
v0.2.0: four-layer extraction (fact/experience/negative/skill) and a stage-2 LLM relevance filter that may only drop candidates.

v0.9.1 GLOBAL KNOWLEDGE BASE: ~/.dsh/global-knowledge holds entries carrying tags + applicable_node_types, queryable across workspaces with knowledge_query. An entry with NEITHER axis never travels — a local lesson stays local, and the per-workspace retrieval gate is untouched.

v0.9.1 DYNAMIC TASK GRAPH: <memoryDir>/task-graph.json. The start node is fixed; the goal node becomes immutable once lock-goal records it (unlock-goal needs a written reason), while paths stay editable. Every accepted edit appends one history entry and writes the reverse anchor into the knowledge base.

v0.9.1 PHASE NUDGE: when the DAG's active node changes, one [系统提示] line names the phase and how much global knowledge applies. It fires once per node — a banner repeated every turn is a banner nobody reads.
